concepts.name: AI-Avatar Commerce
concepts.premise: Users create AI avatars that try on clothes from local boutiques and share looks, earning affiliate commissions.
concepts.wedge: Local boutiques with real inventory but no content engine. The avatar is the content engine.
concepts.primaryLoop: create avatar -> try on garment -> share look -> viewer clicks garment -> viewer signs up to try it on their own avatar -> shares
concepts.monetization: Affiliate commission on attributed boutique sales, split between the sharer and the platform.

rationale.velocity: Two independent rising waves — short-video commerce and generative media — intersect here rather than one carrying the concept alone.
rationale.shareability: The shared artefact is the product. A look has no value held privately, so sharing is the primary action, not an afterthought bolted onto retention.
rationale.retention: Fashion novelty decays fast. Return visits depend on a supply of new drops, which is a partner-operations problem, not a product problem. Scored honestly at 3.
rationale.acquisition: Each shared look is a landing page with intrinsic interest; organic reach is credible but depends on off-platform distribution the app does not control.
rationale.liquidity: Two-sided cold start. Boutique supply must be seeded manually per city; this is the single hardest constraint.
rationale.monetization: Affiliate mechanics are well understood and attribution is solvable, but the take rate is set by boutiques and is thin on low-ticket apparel.

risks.mitigation: Launch one city, 15-25 boutiques, manual onboarding. Treat supply as an operations gate (G2), not a growth assumption.
Avatars are stylised and user-parameterised, never uploaded-face derivatives by default. No automatic body 'idealisation'. Explicit consent before any likeness feature.
Renders are labelled as illustrative try-on, not photographic. Real product imagery shown alongside.
Signed order webhooks, bounded attribution window, immutable commission ledger, self-referral guard.
Shared looks carry a persistent paid-affiliate disclosure; commissions disclosed at point of click.

concepts.name: Micro-Gig Social Network
concepts.premise: A Snapchat-style app where neighbours post quick tasks (e.g. 'fix my tap for $5') and pay via an integrated wallet.
concepts.wedge: Sub-$20 neighbourhood tasks that formal marketplaces cannot serve because their take rate exceeds the job's margin.
concepts.primaryLoop: post task -> neighbour completes -> payment in wallet -> completer posts own task -> invites neighbours for density
concepts.monetization: Wallet float, instant-payout fee, and optional promoted tasks.

rationale.velocity: Gig side hustles are a durable trend rather than a spiking one; durable is good for a business, weaker for a viral wedge.
rationale.shareability: A completed tap repair is not a shareable artefact. Sharing must be manufactured through incentives, which is expensive and fragile.
rationale.retention: Genuine recurring need — household tasks recur weekly without prompting.
rationale.acquisition: Referral works only within a radius; national reach has no compounding value, so acquisition must be re-won city by city.
rationale.liquidity: Hyperlocal double cold start per neighbourhood, the most punishing liquidity shape in marketplaces.
rationale.monetization: Wallet economics require money-transmission licensing, which is a regulatory cost centre before it is a revenue line.

risks.mitigation: Partner with a licensed PSP; do not custody funds directly at MVP.
Identity verification, in-app record of engagement, ratings, and an incident channel before launch.
Single-neighbourhood launch with a seeded supply of vetted completers.
